items.title: Three equivalent characterisations of seminormal schemes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises seminormality of a scheme in three equivalent ways: the scheme is seminormal; it equals its own seminormalization; and every universal homeomorphism onto it which induces isomorphisms on residue fields and has reduced source is an isomorphism. The proof reads the equivalence of the first two off the construction of the seminormalization, derives the second from the third by applying it to the seminormalization morphism, and proves the third from the second by factoring the identity of the scheme through the assumed universal homeomorphism, showing the first arrow of that factorisation is a closed immersion using the section-immersion lemma and separatedness, and concluding it is an isomorphism because it is also bijective on points and its target is reduced.
